plan_review.notes: Reviewer found 2 blocking gaps: (1) router concurrency group lacked queue: max, so GitHub would drop pending events instead of queueing them under burst -- fixed by adding queue: max matching the ci-recovery.yml pattern; (2) TOCTOU race between dispatch and Actions-API visibility across serialized invocations, plus missing pending status -- fixed by adding pending to OUTSTANDING_RUN_STATUSES and a bounded waitForOutstandingCount poll before a dispatching invocation releases its concurrency slot. Both fixes verified by new unit tests.

rounds.notes: Blocking: queue:max unconditionally combined with a cancel-in-progress expression that can be true (flag-off schedule/workflow_dispatch path) -- GitHub rejects that combination, breaking the legacy/rollback path. Fixed by making queue conditional on MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED, matching where cancel-in-progress is guaranteed false. Non-blocking: (1) runFromEnv has no end-to-end test (accepted as pre-existing convention/out of scope), (2) dispatch-cap log used prNumbers.length instead of dispatchable.length (fixed), (3) waitForOutstandingCount comment overstated as airtight (reworded).

Verified blocking fix is genuinely correct (queue and cancel-in-progress expressions are mutually exclusive on MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED), confirmed non-blocking fixes, fresh full-diff pass found no new issues. 47/47 tests passing, lint clean.

Post-merge correction round: removed the trainEnabled->Infinity fallback from computeDispatchBudget per parent-session instruction (protection must not lapse when the merge-train feature is disabled). Reviewer confirmed no remaining path to Infinity, unconditional scheduledPulls fetch preserves routing semantics, trainQueueNonEmpty via queueEntries() is fail-closed, unconditional waitForOutstandingCount is a documented tradeoff, new burst/unit tests correctly replace stale Infinity assertions, and the new residual-limitation handoff section is accurately scoped. 48/48 tests passing, lint clean, verify:fast passed.

Second post-merge correction round: replaced the conditional (train-gated) workflow concurrency block with one fully static/unconditional group (crawler-ci-recovery-router), cancel-in-progress:false, queue:max -- applying to every event type in every mode, closing the residual cross-PR race from the flag-off legacy per-PR groups. Reviewer confirmed: (1) group is a plain string with no expression syntax/branching, achieving true full serialization; (2) cancel-in-progress:false + queue:max is exactly the GitHub-permitted combination, corroborated by the existing ci-recovery.yml pattern; (3) the queue-depth risk (~100 pending runs/group) and loss of schedule/workflow_dispatch cancel-in-progress dedup are explicitly documented as accepted, monitored trade-offs in the handoff, not silent regressions; (4) rewritten workflow-structure tests genuinely parse the real YAML via the yaml package and assert on parsed values, not re-asserted constants; (5) no stale references to the old per-mode group names or MERGE_TRAIN_ENABLED-gated concurrency remain anywhere in the repo outside historical ledger/audit text. 48/48 tests passing, lint clean.
